slub:mscr.dresd.r.310.name: Maya scribes, individual names unrecorded
slub:mscr.dresd.r.310.detail: The holding library distinguishes six hands and gives a probable northern or northeastern Yucatán origin for the surviving manuscript.

slub:mscr.dresd.r.310.name: Johann Christian Götze
slub:mscr.dresd.r.310.detail: Götze described acquiring the manuscript in Vienna in 1739. The 1740 transfer list is a separate record, and the earlier route stays open.

slub:mscr.dresd.r.310.name: Constantin Karl Falkenstein
slub:mscr.dresd.r.310.role: Library conservator and display decision maker
slub:mscr.dresd.r.310.detail: As chief librarian, Falkenstein arranged the two parts between glass panes in 1835. The player tests their documented separate spans on a practice rail.

brooklyn:70.177.69.name: Maker unrecorded
brooklyn:70.177.69.detail: Brooklyn Museum gives a 1400–1532 date range and an Inca attribution. It does not identify the maker of the cotton object.

brooklyn:70.177.69.name: Nobuko Kajatani
brooklyn:70.177.69.role: Researcher credited for the later attribution
brooklyn:70.177.69.detail: The collection credits Kajatani and Anne Rowe for its 1993 Inca attribution. The exercise separates this date from the making range and from what the cords record.

brooklyn:70.177.69.name: Anne Rowe
brooklyn:70.177.69.role: Researcher credited for the later attribution
brooklyn:70.177.69.detail: Rowe shares the 1993 attribution credit. The layout keeps both names on the attribution face.

brooklyn:70.177.69.name: Ernest Erickson
brooklyn:70.177.69.detail: The museum credits Erickson’s gift under the exact accession 70.177.69.

loc:g4701g.ct009133.name: Nahua painter-scribes, individual names unrecorded
loc:g4701g.ct009133.detail: The Library of Congress uses the manuscript’s pictorial conventions as evidence for Indigenous authorship. The surviving sheet also carries Latin-letter glosses.

loc:g4701g.ct009133.name: Lord-11 Quetzalecatzin
loc:g4701g.ct009133.role: Ancestral leader represented in the genealogy
loc:g4701g.ct009133.detail: The Library of Congress describes Quetzalecatzin as a regional leader in 1480. The surviving manuscript was produced much later.

loc:g4701g.ct009133.name: don Alonso and don Matheo
loc:g4701g.ct009133.role: Leaders named in the manuscript’s glosses
loc:g4701g.ct009133.detail: The catalogue essay uses names in the glosses as clues to the colonial-era composition. Those names do not identify the painter-scribes.

loc:g4701g.ct009133.name: John Hessler
loc:g4701g.ct009133.role: Library of Congress curator and modern source author
loc:g4701g.ct009133.detail: Hessler describes the family genealogy, land claims and the supported date range of the surviving sheet in a 2017 Library of Congress essay.

wam:03106.name: Cavendish blacksmith, name unrecorded
wam:03106.detail: The Warren catalogue dates the making to about 1848 and names Cavendish, Vermont as the place of casting. It leaves the blacksmith unnamed.

wam:03106.name: Phineas Gage
wam:03106.detail: Gage is named in the 1850 inscription and donated the iron to the Warren Anatomical Museum that year. The catalogue also records its later return at his request.

wam:03106.name: Hannah Trussell Swetland Gage
wam:03106.role: Custody witness through a recorded handover
wam:03106.detail: Gage’s mother gave the iron to John Martyn Harlow in 1867, a step in the later custody history.

wam:03106.name: John Martyn Harlow
wam:03106.detail: Harlow received the iron in 1867 and donated it to the museum in 1868. These are later custody records.
